I thought this,

That after X years without Y a person is still a Y addict however the label of 'addict' changes from someone who 'has to do Y' into someone who when they start doing Y will keep on doing it for some time after (even if destructive).

By no means am I an expert, but having had multiple family members succumb to their addictions, I can kinda spitball some ideas. My dad's youngest brother got in deep to meth and alcohol. He was in and out of prison most of the time I knew him. Never lead a proper life, never made anything useful of himself. About the best he ever did for the world was have two kids, one who made it and another who's still getting there. He showed up for his father's funeral, and he tried to do right by his mother in the end.

But he was always an addict.

My mother's father was an alcoholic for many years in her early life. By the time I knew the man, he'd been clean for a decade and a half.

But he avoids alcohol like it's acid.

My point being, I think that once you succumb to an addiction, you'll never truly be free of it. It's a part of you that you're going to have to fight for the rest of your life. That doesn't make you an addict, though, in my opinion. My grandfather had an addiction. My uncle was an addict. There's a clear line between the two, in my mind.

My uncle was an addict because no matter how hard he "tried", he always went crawling back to his old vices. In the end, it killed him young. My grandfather had an addiction, but he never allowed himself to give into it after he'd broken its hold for good. He's lived a long, long life. He'll be living for a little while longer too, I'm sure. He fights his addiction, and he beats it, and that, to me, is why he is not an addict.

You sound sincere, so here's my honest advice, if you'll have it.

Don't ever give in again. Whatever you have to do, do it. You came out of a seven year stint in prison with the honest desire to make a positive change in your life. That's rare. You need to take it and run with it, and that monster walking in your shadow? It will only win because you let it. I'm not trying to sell you Jesus or anything, that ain't my thing, but you have to build up your soul. Don't really care how you go about it, but you have to learn to value yourself and your dreams. Find reasons to fight every day, because the moment you stop resisting, you'll slip right back into the drug's arms.

But hey man, lots of people do it. So take it slowly. One day at a time will do. Find some good people to bring into your life.
